text:
Elliot Price: Docs review request: can folks sanity-check the “safe-to-share” wording on the new Known Issues pages before we merge/publish?

Links (drafts):
- Streaming disconnects + reconnect guidance (Hosted/Dedicated)
- 429 throttling + quota misconfig
- Dedicated latency spikes / “noisy neighbor”

PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/642
Confluence mirror plan is in the PR description. Main question: what belongs in public docs vs internal Confluence runbook content.

Wei Chen: Taking a pass now. First reaction: the Streaming page is mostly fine, but we should not mention specific regions/models where we “see this most often” unless it’s a stable, long-lived issue. That line about “primarily us-east during peak” feels like incident leakage.

Priya Shah: +1. Support is going to copy/paste whatever’s on that page into customer threads. If we say “us-east peak” we’ll get “so you know it’s broken” replies.

Kira Thompson: Dedicated latency spike page: “noisy neighbor” language is risky in public docs. It implies multi-tenant interference even though Dedicated is supposed to be isolated.

Elliot Price: Good catch. What wording do we prefer?

Kira Thompson: Maybe frame as “capacity saturation” / “workload burst / autoscaling lag” instead of “noisy neighbor”. And keep the actual diagnostic decision tree (dashboards + threshold numbers) internal.

Wei Chen: Agree. The sections that should stay internal:
- Grafana links / panel names
- alert names + thresholds
- “page SRE if X”
- any mention of specific incident IDs or internal components that are not customer-facing (scheduler shard names, node pools, etc.)

Owen Phillips: Support POV: we still need something actionable for customers in public docs, otherwise it becomes “contact Support” and doesn’t deflect tickets.

Owen Phillips: For Streaming, public doc should include:
- common symptoms
- required log fields to capture (request_id, response headers, sdk version, timeout settings)
- safe client-side mitigations (retry + reconnect patterns, idempotency notes)

Owen Phillips: But internal doc can include the “if disconnect rate > X in region Y check dashboard Z” stuff.

Elliot Price: Makes sense. I can split into:
1) “Customer guidance” section (public)
2) “Internal diagnostics (Support/SRE)” section (Confluence only)

Wei Chen: For 429 page: the “temporary raise limits” paragraph needs guardrails. We should avoid implying we can instantly raise everyone’s quota. Suggest:
- explain how to view current limits in Console
- recommend exponential backoff + jitter
- mention Dedicated as option if sustained throughput requirement
- say “contact Support” for temporary adjustments (no promises)

Monica Patel: SDK note: public doc should be consistent w/ what our SDKs do by default. Right now Python defaults to retries for some 5xx but NOT for 429 unless configured. In the draft we say “SDK retries automatically” which is not universally true.

Elliot Price: Oof, thanks. Can you point me to the current behavior? I’ll update the wording to be precise.

Monica Patel: In Python: `max_retries` defaults to 2, but 429 handling depends on `retry_on` config (we’re changing that in https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk-python/pull/519). I’d say “configure retries” not “automatic”.

Priya Shah: +1 please avoid “automatic”. Support gets pinned when someone’s code isn’t retrying and they thought it was.

Kira Thompson: Dedicated latency spike page also currently says “ask us to move you to a quieter pool” (paraphrasing). That should not be in public docs. Internal-only, and even then it’s a last resort.

Elliot Price: Yep, removing that. Public version: “If you have Dedicated and see sustained p95 latency increases under steady load, contact Support with timestamps + request_ids. We may recommend scaling policy adjustments or capacity changes.”

Wei Chen: Streaming page: in the “Workarounds” section, suggest we explicitly state safe timeout ranges and that customers should avoid setting read timeouts lower than their max generation window.

Owen Phillips: Please keep it generic (not exact seconds) unless we’re confident. We’ve had customers latch onto “set 60s” and then their prompts exceed it.

Wei Chen: Fair. Maybe: “Set client read timeout comfortably above your typical completion time; if using streaming, keep the connection open and handle partial chunks.”

Elliot Price: Done.

Priya Shah: Another “safe-to-share” rule: avoid telling customers to “pin to model X.Y.Z” unless we’ve validated it’s actually available to them + it’s not a rollback we can’t sustain. Better: “if you’re pinned to a version and see regressions, try rolling forward/back to a nearby supported version; contact Support if you need help identifying compatible versions.”

Elliot Price: I’ll adjust the model pinning section to be “supported versions” + “contact Support for availability”.

Alex Martinez: Jumping in late — +1 to the split approach. In public docs we should avoid anything that implies:
- an incident is ongoing
- specific regions are unreliable
- we guarantee a mitigation timeline

Alex Martinez: But we *can* be concrete about client behavior (reconnect, backoff, idempotency) and what metadata we need.

Wei Chen: Also, on the 429 page, can we add a short callout: “429 != server error; it’s a signal to slow down”? Customers interpret it as “Redwood is down”.

Owen Phillips: Love that. Support has to explain that constantly.

Elliot Price: Added a callout box.

Kira Thompson: Where are we landing on “public vs Confluence” for the decision trees?

Elliot Price: Proposal:
- Public: symptoms, probable causes (high level), safe mitigations, what to send Support
- Internal Confluence: decision tree + screenshots, dashboards, exact fields, escalation triggers, owners

Priya Shah: Works for me. Also tag internal sections “Restricted” if they mention enterprise/private customers, even if anonymized.

Elliot Price: Yep. I’ll add a banner in Confluence: “Internal only. Do not paste into customer threads.”

Wei Chen: Last nit: Dedicated latency spike page uses “noisy neighbor” ~6 times. Please nuke all instances.

Elliot Price: :thumbsup: Replacing with “capacity saturation / scaling lag” throughout.

Monica Patel: Once the docs wording is updated, I’ll sync the SDK PR text to point to the doc page and make sure we don’t oversell default retries.

Elliot Price: Great. I’ll push edits to PR 642 in the next hour and re-request review.

Owen Phillips: Thanks. Once merged, we’ll link these from the Support macros library (INT-1338) but only after the “safe-to-share” bits are final.

Elliot Price: Perfect. I’ll also add the “safe-to-share” flag in the known-issues index and mark these three as shareable w/ the public section only.

Wei Chen: Approved direction. Ping me when the new commit is up and I’ll do a quick final pass.

Elliot Price: Will do.
